questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To see something different, to learn about new cultures etc... It was crucial for me to see new aspects of the francophonie.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit hard about the course catalogue I changed my courses a few times, and the bureaucratic process was sometimes a bit stressing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of assistance from the BRI, they were very helpfull, still somethings about the course list was a hard process. But I'm very thankfull for the Bureau des Relations International, they helped me a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, but I got ripped off from the first place, afterwards the BRI helped me find a new place and from there it was more quite in my housing situation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Not take the cheapest rent, but actually find out which areas are good to live in and maybe meet the persons before you move in. Maybe actually wait to arrive in Guyana before finding a place. Try couchsurfing or Airbnb in the beginning. Live in Montabo, Baduel, qurtier Hibiscus or Remire in the beginning and talk with people before finding a place. Maybe choose a good collocation in Rémire and find a way of mooving around. Maybe a car if it's rain season.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was also a bit long process. I had been a student for a month and a half before actually being registered at my institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: BRI, and yourself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successfull thanks to my very cool home institution.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know maybe talk with the BRI, and insist a lot when you talk to the accueil.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting courses, but a bit low level in some of the courses. But I learned a lot and was very glad that I could choose my own courses quite freely.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A bit low level in the english courses for instance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's a bit more the french way. Some of the teachers were just reading from a book for you to copy in your book, very different from my home institution. In Guyana there are less courses and a lot of travaux dirigé in the end of the semester with presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A rental car that cost me 7000 but its good to have a car or to share a car with somebody if you want to get 10 km or more out of town, and you would want that because there is so much to see!!!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: everything was more expensive than i thought. Food, etc...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: different talent shows some culture festivals a lot of sport if you are into that, travels to iles du salut or marais de kaw.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the sport at uni is cool, some marathons are held during the year in kourou and cayenne. Go out in nature and do some sentier at night, maybe get to know some other young people working in nature associations, they do a lot of outings in nature to see animals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Iles du salut, marais de kaw, saint laurent du maronie and go with a pirog to grand santi and fly home, saül, do some sentier, go to ilet la mere or iles du grand connetable, go to brazil in Oyapock, go see cacao d'amazonie, go take a beer with friends at ole la terre, fifties or cocosoda (le food truck peruvien in Montabo), go enjoy a beer and see Jeune Gueule brewery, go to Kourou. Go to Suriname. walk around in the city center and go for museums and take a drink at les palmistes. go to the beach, watch some sea turtles. go kite surfing, go biking. go to sentiers at night and see snakes with a frontal torch.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I tried the first month but gave up after a month living with a brazilian and a girl from Haiti. I moved in with Pedro (the spanish Erasmus coordinator) and there I found more peace, thanks to him.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, go eat lunch with them hang out at the uni, and do some university sports, you can find info in (Bureau de la vie étudiante (BVE)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The traffic, waiting in lines, the food, socialising with brazilians or people who were different than me. People live a lot in communities here, so the western people are together, the brazilians are together, the spanish people are together the haitians are together and so on.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The difference is so huge, it's so diverse and you learn a lot about so many different cultures. it's very interesting. Guyana is so diverse culturally and in the languages. More than 40 languages are spoken in this territory, if you walk around 1 day in Cayenne you will hear over 15 languages in average.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a good place to stay with people you like, find a way of travelling around (a car can be useful if it's rain season) the university will provide you a bike for free for your stay And be curious about all the stories there is to find on this great territory, there are so many cultures and so many backgrounds= many interesting stories and way of doing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You must go in nature here, even if you are not a nature guy or girl, try to go in the rainforest because it's 97 % of the territory.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It's hard to choose one, Iles du salut, Marais de Kaw, the anthropology course was very interesting. The friends i met here. The kindness of Pedro and Maelle working at the BRI.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was to walk in the rainforest and not to be scared of snakes. But by doing it and watching others do it you actually realise how normal it is and how it's not dangerous at all.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
